items.title: The Odyssey Box Office Drops Just 19% as Its Second Weekend in Theaters Brings Another $215 Million Globally
items.description: Director Christoper Nolan's The Odyssey has managed to track down another $215.3 million at the global box office, dropping only 19% in its second weekend in theaters.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Director Christoper Nolan's The Odyssey has managed to track down another $215.3 million at the global box office, dropping only 19% in its second weekend in theaters.

It's yet another surprisingly strong weekend for the Matt Damon-led epic that saw it wrangle $128.3 million internationally and $87 million domestically. Its total box office haul now stands at $639.6 million, representing only the slightest hit to the already staggering momentum it set sail with upon its July 17, 2026, premiere.

IGN reported that its opening weekend managed to surpass expectations with an impressive $264.1 million debut. Audiences have continued to fill theaters – including the few locations supporting 70mm Imax – through the following week. The split of the total puts The Odyssey at $353.26 internationally and $286.37 domestically, and as the numbers continue to pile, it shouldn't be long before Universal and Nolan reach that illustrious $1 billion milestone.

Speaking of movies hitting $1 billion, although Toy Story 5 was knocked to third in the global box office behind Chinese picture All Wishes Come True, the Pixar film finally managed to reach that billion marker itself. Its worldwide total now positions it with $1.022 billion after spending six weekends in theaters since its June 19 debut.

Stephen Chow's Kung Fu Soccer came in fourth at the box office with a worldwide pull for the weekend of $32.1 million, while Minions & Monsters stuck around in the top five with $28.2 million. Disney's live-action Moana, meanwhile, has failed to catch any wind, coming in sixth at the global box office as its total coasts at an underwhelming $228.16 million. The adaptation is now drifting through its third weekend in theaters after its July 10 premiere saw it barely surpass Disney's recent Snow White movie.

The Odyssey has proven to be the latest critical and commercial success story of 2026. Low-budget horror movies Backrooms and Obsession attracted audiences in the spring, with Toy Story 5 helping to carry the torch as summer began. As the Nolan film is set to continue its run in theaters for a while yet, it seems prepped to finish strong.

While The Odyssey has proven to be quite the contender against the vocal naysayers leading up to its release, it will have some fierce competition next weekend when Marvel unleashes its Spider-Man: Brand New Day. As fans line up to see the next chapter of the Marvel Cinematic Universe and finally uncover the identity of Sadie Sink's mystery character, it's sure to do big numbers when it premieres, too.

Variety reported that The Odyssey had a production budget of about $250 million, with marketing costs estimated to be around $125 million. For more, you can read about the film's recent leak and what Universal did to stop it. You can also see why IGN called it a "pretty great moviegoing experience" in our 8/10 review.

items.title: These Incredible Avengers: Doomsday Figures Give Us a Better Look at the Film's X-Men Costumes | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Hot Toys' Avengers: Doomsday figures have been revealed, giving us a much better look at key X-Men characters like Ian McKellen's Magneto and Channing Tatum's Gambit.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Marvel's Comic-Con panel seems to have opened the floodgates in terms of Avengers: Doomsday merchandise, as multiple companies have now revealed the action figures and collectibles they'll be releasing alongside the film this December. That includes Hot Toys. And, true to form, these incredibly detailed figures are giving us our best look yet at key Doomsday characters like Ian McKellen's Magneto and Channing Tatum's Gambit.

Check out the slideshow gallery below to see the first wave of Hot Toys' Avengers: Doomsday figures:

Hot Toys' initial lineup of figures includes James Marsden's Cyclops, Robert Downey, Jr.'s Doctor Doom, Channing Tatum's Gambit, and Ian McKellen's Magneto. Doom will also be getting a separate throne accessory. It's worth noting that Sideshow Collectibles' Comic-Con booth also has figures of Patrick Stewart's Professor Xavier, Kelsey Grammer's Beast, and a Sentinel on display, but those figures haven't gone live for preorder yet.

This is definitely our best look yet at McKellen in his latest (and presumably final) appearance as the Master of Magnetism. Fittingly, McKellen's costume looks to be his most heavily comic-inspired one yet, complete with the red and purple helmet and red suit.

As for Tatum's Gambit, things haven't changed too much from his previous appearance in 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine, though this costume appears to be a bit darker and more muted to suit the grittier tone of Doomsday.

All of these 1:6 scale figures will be released in both standard and Deluxe Edition versions, with the latter including more accessories and more elaborate display bases. The Deluxe Cyclops even comes with a removable leather jacket for that peak '90s X-Men look.

These figures will all be released between October 2026 and December 2027. The non-deluxe Doom figure is an "Early Access" release guaranteed to come out in time for the movie. You can find preorder links for everything below:

Preorder Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday Figures

  • Cyclops
  • Doctor Doom
  • Doom's Throne
  • Gambit
  • Magneto

For more on Avengers: Doomsday, check out the biggest mysteries following Marvel's Comic-Con panel and learn why Marvel was never going to introduce the new X-Men cast this year.

items.title: Universal Responds After All 3 Hours of The Odyssey Leak on Social Media
items.description: Universal has stepped in after a high-quality upload of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey leaked on X/Twitter.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Universal has stepped in after a high-quality upload of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey leaked on X/Twitter.

While viewers headed to theaters to catch the Greek epic on its second weekend at the box office, some stayed home to watch it instead. All two hours and 53 minutes of the blockbuster movie managed to leak onto social media over the weekend, giving thousands access to an astonishingly high-quality (but still inferior) version of the film to watch from the comfort of their homes or, god forbid, their phones.

Most, if not all, uploads across X have seemingly been removed in one way or another, with the most popular post taken down entirely. The responses to The Odyssey leak, however, remain, revealing a mix of reactions from users who were surprised to see the movie posted in its entirety with little fanfare. Others have taken the opportunity to have a bit more fun.

The Odyssey 2026 📺🎞️🎬🍿*

Rotten Tomatoes 🍅: 94%

IMDb: 8.5/10

Fantasy | Action | Adventure • pic.twitter.com/p8LFA2w6ww

— Antonio😈 (@Antonio_aj3) July 26, 2026

"Watching The Odyssey for the first time via a Twitter leak on my iPhone in a small subscreen up top while scrolling my timeline, just as Nolan intended," one user joked.

"Gets taken down the second I start watching it," another said with a "loudly crying" emoji.

As reported by Variety, The Odyssey leak had garnered more than 2.1 million views by the time Universal was finally able to have it taken down. Although it swiftly stepped in, it seems the posts were live long enough for people to watch huge chunks of the film.

"We became aware of the unauthorized posting of the film and immediately initiated takedown protocols," Universal told the site in a statement. "We take copyright infringement seriously and will pursue all appropriate remedies to protect our content and intellectual property rights."

Despite the X community getting their hands on an early upload, The Odyssey leak probably won't do much to slow its success in theaters. Its opening weekend saw Nolan bring home his best global debut ever with a worldwide total of 264.1 million, with its second weekend already piling on even more impressive stats. Meanwhile, X overseer Elon Musk said his AI tool Grok would be able to make its own version of The Odyssey before the end of 2026. He said this AI-generated version of the story will be "historically accurate and true to the art of Homer."

Nolan famously went to great lengths to ensure his The Odyssey would be shot entirely using Imax cameras, making this weekend's leak even more disappointing to see. Although fans have flocked from around the country to catch it in their preferred format, Imax CEO Richard Gelfond has said building more 70mm Imax projectors is "not practical."

items.title: Marvel Knew David Jonsson Would Be the Next Black Panther 6 Months Ago After 'Secret Meeting' With Ryan Coogler
items.description: Marvel Studios knew David Jonsson would star in Black Panther 3 'five or six months' ago thanks to a 'secret meeting' director Ryan Coogler Held with Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) boss Kevin Feige.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Marvel Studios knew David Jonsson would star in Black Panther 3 'five or six months' ago thanks to a 'secret meeting' director Ryan Coogler Held with Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) boss Kevin Feige.

The MCU mastermind spoke about the casting process during a conversation with Empire at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026. During their post-Hall H chat, Feige recalled the moment Coogler reached out to pitch the idea of Jonsson leading Black Panther 3 as the next Black Panther.

The Marvel Studios head said an official search for an actor to play the son of the late Chadwick Boseman's character, T'Challa, when Coogler initially got in touch. Although the director was busy at the time, it sounds like Jonsson has been on his mind for months.

"I’ll give you the real scoop," Feige said. "We hadn’t started a search yet. Ryan was working on Sinners, and when Ryan works on a project he’s all in. So the presumption very much was we would sit with him after Sinners came out, after the Academy campaign. We were waiting 'til after the Academy Awards to sit with Ryan and begin that process.

"A month and a half or so before that process, he called me and said, 'I found him.' I said, 'What do you mean?' He goes, 'I found him. He's this guy, David Jonsson.' He mentioned his movies. I had seen some of them. I watched more. He goes, 'I'm going to meet him.'"

Jonsson is a British actor and has been a rising star in Hollywood for the last few years. First starring in lesser-known roles with projects like Endeavour and Deep State, the actor eventually went on to receive praise for his time as Andy the android in 2024's Alien: Romulus. Last year, he nailed another standout part as Peter in the live-action adaptation of Stephen King's The Long Walk.

His time on screens big and small caught Coogler's attention, and as of Marvel Studios' Hall H panel last night, he's set to be the next Black Panther. When he shows up in Black Panther 3, he'll be joined by Letitia Wright as Shuri and Winston Duke as M'Baku. Feige said Jonsson's inclusion is a casting choice Coogler and the rest of Marvel have kept secret longer than some might have guessed.

"He had a secret meeting with him under cloak of darkness in a hotel somewhere, and called me afterwards and said, 'He's the guy, he's the guy, I felt it. I felt it in my soul. He's a good man, and he is the next Black Panther,'" Feige added. "And I got chills, and I got a little welled-up and said, 'Let’s do it.' So we've been sitting on this secret for a good five or six months."

Black Panther 3 premieres December 15, 2028. For more, you can read about how Ryan Gosling finally landed the part of Ghost Rider. You can also catch up on everything else announced during the Marvel Hall H panel.

items.title: George Takei and Other Star Trek Alumni Celebrate 60 Years and Name Trek's Greatest Lessons | Comic Con 2026
items.description: At San Diego Comic-Con 2026, George Takei and cast members across generations celebrated 60 years of Star Trek, reflecting on Gene Roddenberry's enduring vision.
items.author: Eric Goldman
items.content:
On Saturday, San Diego Comic-Con held a celebration for Star Trek in Hall H as the iconic sci-fi series — and the franchise it begat — turns 60 this year.

A large panel did a commendable job representing many Star Trek series across many eras, including Michael Dorn (The Next Generation, Deep Space Nine, Picard), Robert Picardo (Voyager, Prodigy, Starfleet Academy), Dominic Keeting (Enterprise), Cirroc Lofton (Deep Space Nine), Doug Jones (Discovery), Michelle Hurd (Picard), Jerry O'Connell (Lower Decks), Christina Chong (Strange New Worlds), and Karim Diané (Starfleet Academy). And last but certainly not least was the legendary George Takei, representing the original Star Trek series.

It's a bit of an odd time for the Star Trek, with some already-produced seasons of completed series Star Trek: Strange New Worlds and Star Trek: Starfleet Academy left to air. Beyond that, nothing has been announced on the TV front. A new Trek film is in development from Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley, but obviously, plenty of movie attempts have been made in the past decades that didn't come to fruition. Still, when the very well-edited opening montage — filled with clips from Star Trek series and films from the past 60 years — concluded with the voiceover "The journey will never be over,” you knew that would certainly turn out to be true, whatever the next step turns out to be.

Asked by moderator Scott Mantz about seeing the legacy of Star Trek endure so long, Takei spoke about how honored he felt to be part of what's turned into such a long legacy that resulted from a three-season show that struggled to stay on the air at the time, noting the multi-generational younger actors surrounding him on the stage.

Diané, the most recent actor on the panel to join Trek, said he very quickly was overwhelmed by the passion and dedication of the fanbase, recounting a fan who showed him a tattoo he'd gotten of his character, Jay-Den Kraag, on his leg.

"Seeing my face on a grown man’s thigh… that’s permanent!" Diané said.

Michael Dorn, who was part of the first risky attempt to continue Star Trek with a new cast beyond the original series, said that the long term impact of The Next Generation and everything since "was a shock to all of us... That we still are viable and they're making more shows about this one thing."

All the actors who joined Trek after those first two series said they felt the impact of it, with the ever-busy Doug Jones — known for playing characters in elaborate makeup in projects like Hellboy and Pan's Labyrinth — saying he had always lamented not getting to do so a Star Trek series, only for the franchise to return to TV after a long break with Star Trek: Discovery, where he had a major role as Saru.

Jerry O'Connell recounted how much it meant to him when he immediately got a text from his Stand By Me co-star Wil Wheaton, after it was announced he'd been cast in the animated series Star Trek: Lower Decks. Wheaton, of course, played Wesley Crusher on The Next Generation, and O'Connell recalled the text simply saying, “Welcome to Starfleet, Commander."

Many of the panelists lauded Star Trek and its creator, Gene Roddenberry, for how progressive and ahead of its time the franchise was from the start in 1966, with its groundbreaking depiction of a bridge crew who were made up of many difference races and backgrounds, giving viewers an optimistic look at the future. Michelle Hurd said it has a huge impact on her and her sisters to see the late Nichelle Nichols as Uhura, playing the kind of role a Black woman rarely had at that time. Hurd got very emotional, saying how much it meant to her to be sitting on the panel right next to Takei, someone who was also a part of that iconic first crew.

As the panel wrapped up, Takei was asked which part of Roddenberry's vision of Star Trek is the most important to today as far as lessons that could be learned. Takei said what stood out for him the most was the Vulcan philosophical belief in the concept of IDIC: infinite diversity in infinite combinations.

Takei explained how he felt that as important as it was for Star Trek to represent people who physically look different from one another, he also felt there was importance and strength in acknowledging and learning from the diverse backgrounds as well.

"It's the history. It's what differences we bring other than the visual," Takei said. "We have a whole history that has shaped our vantage point on life and how we see life. And it's recognizing that [history] among all of us, coming together, and realizing that our strength is in our working together. We have various thoughts that are exchanged, we have maybe different reactions to what is said, but it's our recognition of that difference and the courage and the boldness to think about that difference and learn from it. I think that's what the strength of Star Trek is: infinite diversity in different combinations... And then to live long and prosper."

Photo credit: Chris Delmas / AFP via Getty Images

items.title: Reacher Star Alan Ritchson Confirms Conversations With DC About Playing 'Another Character' That Isn't Batman
items.description: Reacher star Alan Ritchson has confirmed he won't be playing Batman in the DCU, but he has had conversations with DC about playing "another character" instead.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Reacher star Alan Ritchson has confirmed he won't be playing Batman in the DCU, but he has had conversations with DC about playing "another character" instead.

Ritchson touched on the rumors that he could portray the next iteration of the Caped Crusader during a Reacher panel at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026 (via CinemaBlend). His thoughts on the matter follow years of hopeful fancasts as the DCU carves out its corner of the movie universe with a new Superman, a new Gotham, and eventually, a new Batman.

Ritchson didn't quite outright deny that he would play Bruce Wayne in the DCU, but it sounds like the chances of it happening any time soon are slim. Still, it appears he and DC will have each other's phones ringing for a long time to come.

"I feel like I have to address this because it comes up all the time," Ritchson said. "I don't ever want to lead somebody on to feel like, 'Maybe he's…' I've had a lot of conversations with DC about what to do because we would like to work together. I still never say never – maybe Batman is in the future – but I don't think it is."

Ritchson has been addressing rumors that he would play Bruce Wayne in the DCU for years. He seemed amused by the idea when it was brought up in 2023, although he dodged mentioning any potential conversations about actually portraying the character. Then, in August of 2025, the Reacher actor confirmed he had spoken with DC but cast doubt on being Batman.

Fans started to get their hopes up yet again when Ritchson beat around the bush on Happy, Sad, Confused last week, but at SDCC 2026 he downplayed his chances of playing Batman once again. However, it sounds like there is at least one character both he and DC have in mind.

"We're having conversations about another character," he teased. "I just don't think Batman is in the cards for me, as much as I would love to do it."

Ritchson mentioning conversations of playing "another character" drew lots of oohs and aahs from the SDCC crowed – but who is this mystery superhero/supervillain? For now, Ritchson is keeping his lips sealed, but with the DC barreling forward every day, it hopefully won't be too long before we hear more.

While the DCU's Batman has not been (publicly) cast, DC will at least introduce viewers to its new Gotham when its Clayface movie comes to theaters later this year. We can at least hope to learn more as DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran move closer to releasing their Batman: The Brave and the Bold project in the future. The Batman Part 2 should help with the wait in the meantime.

Photo by Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images.

items.title: Kevin Feige Says Ryan Gosling Approached Him With a 'Specific Vision' for Ghost Rider in the MCU
items.description: Ryan Gosling will officially star in a Ghost Rider movie in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and according to MCU orchestrator Kevin Feige, he's already got a "specific vision" in mind for the character.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Ryan Gosling will officially star in a Ghost Rider movie in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and according to MCU orchestrator Kevin Feige, he's already got a "specific vision" in mind for the character.

The Marvel Studios boss spoke about Gosling's love for the Spirit of Vengeance during a post-Hall H interview with ComicBook at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026. We've known the Project Hail Mary star has wanted to play Ghost Rider for some time, but it sounds like Gosling has had his take on the character mentally mapped out for a while.

Feige played coy when asked if Gosling would portray Johnny Blaze or Danny Ketch in the movie. Just moments removed from the big SDCC panel, it's no surprise to see Marvel playing it safe, but he was still willing to share at least a little bit about how the MCU Ghost Rider came to be.

"I am going to let Ryan reveal what he wants to reveal when he wants to reveal it, and what he wanted to reveal today was he's playing Ghost Rider," Fiege said with a smile.

"He's a huge fan of the comics. He did come to us, particularly with a specific vision based on some particular comics, but I'll let him unveil that as he wants to."

Gosling has been the rumored pick for a previously unannounced Ghost Rider movie for years. However, it wasn't until the actor confirmed he had spoken with Marvel Studios about playing the motorcycle-riding fireball that fans truly started to get their hopes up.

"We'll keep hope alive," Gosling told Happy, Sad, Confused in March. "Some discussions have been had. It's a complicated situation."

What those "discussions" involved might be particularly interesting for comic book readers, who will no doubt be revisiting some of the most iconic Ghost Rider stories as the movie moves forward. For now, we'll have to wait for Gosling and Feige to share more about how the MCU will bring in Johnny Blaze, Danny Ketch, or maybe someone else.

As announced last night, Ghost Rider is set to ride into theaters in 2028. It will be directed by Deadpool & Wolverine director Shawn Levy and written by Star Wars: Starfighter scribe Jonathan Tropper. Until then, you can check out everything Marvel Studios announced at its SDCC Hall H panel.

items.title: Resident Evil Director Knows RE2 Didn't Have Snow or iPhones, But He 'Took Liberties' to Make the Movie Better
items.description: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has seen all the comments about the snow and iPhones in his new movie, but he said he's got a good reason for why he "took liberties" with the lore.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has seen all the comments about the snow and iPhones in his new movie, but he said he's got a good reason for why he "took liberties" with the lore.

Cregger has spent some of his time at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026 celebrating the release of his movie's new trailer. He's also used his presence at the show to talk more about why his version of the Raccoon City Incident looks different from what fans of games like Resident Evil 2 and 3 might have expected.

"I take liberties," he told IGN. "It's not 1998. It takes place in modern times. I know that, during the events of Resident Evil 2, it's not snowing, and yet, in this movie, I thought it would be better for the story and for the visual, you know, whatever I'm doing, if it was snowy. It's going to be a better movie for it.

"I am not trying to adapt a video game. I'm not using the characters from the games. I'm not telling a story that the games tell because I'm not going to be able to do it better than the games. The games are so well executed, and to me, Leon and Claire and these characters, they exist so perfectly in the games that anyone I cast and any difference that I do with them would be, probably, to the detriment of what I was trying to do."

Most fans would agree; mixing the director behind Barbarian and Weapons into the Resident Evil universe feels like a recipe for success. Although the premiere of its first trailer largely kept the hype momentum going, it's also safe to say it's picked up a few critics along the way.

Some were quick to point out that, while the original lore saw the Raccoon City Incident take place in the late '90s in a rainy town on the brink of destruction, Cregger's film seemed to be set in a more modern, wintry timeline. Despite a plethora of references to elements and moments that should feel familiar to fans, the criticism from the more skeptical watchers has only simmered the last few months.

Cregger has already spent the time leading up to the Resident Evil movie proclaiming his love for games like Resident Evil 2 and 4, while also doing his best to calm uneasy watchers. Now, he's doing his best to put fears to rest entirely.

"It's kind of like when you have your favorite book, and then you find out someone is turning your favorite book into a movie, and then you hear who they cast, and you're always like, 'Not that. No. That's not what I want.' I'm not trying to do that," Cregger explained. "What I'm trying to do is make a Resident Evil movie that really is a love letter to the experience of playing a Resident Evil game. To me, that means a couple of different things."

He said his vision for a Resident Evil movie needs things like the T-Virus, Umbrella Corporation, and Raccoon City. Pieces of the puzzle like this are "necessary," which is why, instead of seeing Leon quip one-liners with star Austin Abrams, fans are far more likely to see that classic red-and-white logo pop up.

"They're in there, but the most important thing I'm trying to do is make a movie that feels like it's unraveling the way that, when you play the game, it's unfolding," Cregger continued. "To me, that means a couple of different things. It's about one character moving on foot from point A to point B, moving from set piece to set piece, location to location.

"Every location has its own unique threat, right? You have to keep in mind resource management and your health. You're wounded, and you feel like you never have enough ammunition, and the world is always too big for you, and yet somehow, you've got to make it through, right? That's what I'm trying to do."

The most recent Resident Evil movie trailer showed more of Abrams' courier character while teasing some of the other connections to the wider universe. Like the first clip, it had its fans and its critics, as the footage reminded viewers of its modern settings and lore tweaks. Cregger has said that, when the film finally premieres, those who are most familiar with the series should feel right at home.

"It's like, if this movie was a Resident Evil game, call it Resident Evil 10, it wouldn't feel weird. You know what I mean? That's what I'm trying to build."

Cregger finalized his response to concerned fans by saying he gets why so many are upset. Resident Evil means so much to so many people, and the franchise's movies have mostly strayed from the source material, but that's why this movie will blend its lore with the true feel of a survival horror adventure.

"I get the instinct to dig in," Cregger said. "I'll be honest: I've never seen a Resident Evil movie because they don't look, to me, like what I love so much about the games that I play. I was just like, 'Not my Resident Evil.' So, I understand that attitude. I'm making this because I want a movie to exist that feels like the experience of playing the game, and so, I was able to do that. That's what I'm doing."

Cregger's Resident Evil movie comes to theaters September 18, 2026. While we wait for Cregger to share more, you can check out why a completely different group of fans went after the trailer. You can also read about how Abrams almost met an untimely fate on set.

items.title: Kevin Feige Pushes Back at Criticisms That Dr. Doom Hasn't Had Thanos-Level Buildup
items.description: Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige is hitting back at Doomsday critics who feel like Dr. Doom hasn’t had the necessary buildup to crown him the next big bad of the MCU in the way that Thanos was back in the days of Infinity War.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige is hitting back at Doomsday critics who feel like Dr. Doom hasn’t had the necessary buildup to crown him the next big bad of the MCU in the way that Thanos was back in the days of Infinity War.

It’s a conversation that’s been brewing on social media in the weeks leading up to Comic Con, and now that Marvel’s highly-anticipated Hall H panel has concluded, it’s boiling over.

After the panel, Feige was directly asked about his thoughts on the idea that, compared to Thanos’ arc in the Infinity Saga, Victor Von Doom just hasn’t had the necessary screentime to build himself up as the major villain that Avengers: Doomsday is making him out to be.

In response, the Marvel prez referenced the countless memes that cropped up after Thanos’ post-credits scenes in Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, and Age of Ultron, saying that fans at the time felt he wasn’t doing much of anything.

“The Thanos buildup has built up in people’s heads over the years,” he said in a carpet interview with Brandon Davis. “He sat on a chair at the end. He put on a gauntlet and said, ‘I’ll do it myself.’ And he yelled at Ronin on a video screen briefly. I remember the memes making fun of Thanos. ‘He’s just sitting in a chair.’ There was a Twitter feed updating every day, ‘I’m still sitting in my chair.’ It was more clever than that, it was funny.”

"I remember the memes making fun of Thanos. 'He's just sitting in a chair.'"

Then Feige dropped a hint that shed a bit more light on the future of the MCU; Doom will be officially introduced in Doomsday in the same way Thanos was fully introduced in Endgame.

“When we got to Infinity War we said, ‘This is really the introduction of Thanos the people.’ That’s how that movie was built. That’s what we’re doing with Doom. Doomsday is an introduction to the story of Doom. You peel the onion, you learn things about him as you go. It’s very much meant for audiences that know and love him from the comics and audiences who have no clue who he is,” he continued.

Kevin Feige addresses fans saying that Doctor Doom has no buildup compared to Thanos:

“The Thanos buildup has built up in people’s heads over the years. He sat on a chair at the end. He put on a gauntlet and said, ‘I’ll do it myself.’ And he yelled at Ronin on a video screen… pic.twitter.com/87nXC1WvL6

— Avengers Updates (@AvengersUpdated) July 26, 2026

It’s highly likely that the fight against Doom doesn’t stop in Doomsday, and that we will have several more films in between the major battles exploring new stories within the MCU.

Marvel is certainly building up Doomsday to be their next big hit, though, given the sheer size of the film’s cast, many of whom showed up to the Hall H Panel. Of those who turned up, the next Black Panther, David Jonsson, was also in attendance, who made his big reveal for Black Panther III to the cheers of thousands of excited fans.

A new Ghost Rider movie was revealed, as well, with Ryan Gosling confirmed to play the titular role. Other than that, no major news was revealed — but with Spider-Man: Brand New Day releasing later this month and D23 happening in August, it’s possible we could see more of Marvel’s plans in the coming weeks.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.description: At Apple TV's first ever Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con, the cast and crew of Widow's Bay reacted to the show's breakout success.
items.author: Leanne Butkovic

In the middle of a hefty two-hour panel that marked Apple TV's first Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con, the cast and creators of Widow's Bay popped in to reflect on the show's breakout success, which includes 19 recent Emmy nominations. "Dale, I think you had the best reaction," series creator Katie Dippold said to Dale Dickey, who earned one of those Emmy nods for Supporting Actress as Rosemary. "'Dear God in heaven, what the hell just happened,'" Dickey recalled.

Joining Dippold and Dickey on the stage was director Hiro Murai, Stephen Root (Wyck), Jeff Hiller (Dale), K Callan (Ruth), Kevin Carroll (Bashir), and Kingston Rooney Southwick (Evan). (Sadly, no Kate O'Flynn, who plays the fan favorite city hall aide Patricia.)

"It’s amazing it became a watercolor show," Root said, reacting to a question from the moderator, Happy Sad Confused podcast host Josh Horowitz, about the show building up to a zeitgeist-y must-watch. "The tone for he show is everything," he said not long after when they were asked about the series' blend of horror and comedy. "If you get the tone of the show, you’re gonna get the show."

"I feel like every time I did something wrong, they’d say ‘don’t do that,’ and that was a good guardrail," Hiller (half) joked about keeping that sensibility in check.

"I go back to initial conviction — Katie would be like, ‘I know this sounds psychotic, but I would stay at that haunted inn. I would want to get a coffee at that diner," Murai said regarding the grounded feeling of the series despite the terrors of the island. "It should be off-putting to be there, but there’s an inherent coziness. You love this place."

"I would like to be killed there," Dippold said to an appreciative audience.

The cast was asked about each of their characters. Root said that he had "played a lot of heavies" in his life but felt that he could bring "some humanity" to the salty townie Wyck. "You have to see how tirelessly he’s trying to protect the people on the island," he said. "I love being myself a little more in this role than in a lot of other roles I've done. I think it’s about kindness, it really is."

As for Carroll, who plays the exhausted town sheriff whose wife goes into labor during the harrowing season finale, he said the question for his character Bashir is "does he want to be sheriff" of the island? "I think so," Carroll (unexpectedly, to be honest) said. "He's fighting tof his child. What parent in here wou'dnt go to the nth degree for the sake of their children?"

Another major reveal at the end of the first season was an answer to a mystery about how K Callan's Ruth is related to both the founding of the island and Tom and his son Evan. "I knew nothing," Callan said when asked about how clued in she was to Ruth's role. "I got to read the pilot and that was it. I had no idea what Ruth’s journey was going to be. I just put my life in Katie and Hiro’s hand, and thank goodness."

Southwick talked about the importance of the rocky father-son relationship between Evan and Matthew Rhys' Tom. "I think the relationship is so great, because we keep a lot of secrets from each other, and I think that's what kind of keeps us honest," he said. "Certain things that I can do, he can't say that I can't do, because he's doing things that he shouldn't be doing either."

Toward the end of the Widow's Bay time slot, Dickey pulled up a projector screen, recreating a now-iconic scene where Rosemary goes over her geneological findings for the Tom, Patricia, Wyck trio to put an end to the island's bloodlust, that had an old newspaper headline about cannibalism. “It started with cannibalism... right, mayor?" Dickey said, before the screens cut to a live video call from Rhys.

"No, no, you know we don’t talk about cannibalism," joked Rhys, who acknowledged that his mayor is maybe more enthusiastic about managing the island than he is actually proficient at it. "I think his effectiveness would be down to the island to judge," he said. "I think his enthusiasm is without question. He wants the very best for the islandand those who live upon it."

Rhys was also asked about finding the slapstick physicality of his performance as Tom ("I didn’t find anything, Josh, that’s how I live my life") and specifically in Episode 5 as a high-strung, straight-laced goverment leader who happened to take a dose of diabolical-looking mushrooms in Episode 5. "You know, about three to four bottles of good chablis will get you to that place. Which is to be encouraged at times," Rhys said. "It was a lot of fun. YouTube is a great provider these days for acting. I shamelessly copied people enjoying themselves, and that to me was the mushroom trip."

After hanging up with Rhys, Horowitz asked what was most fun to see people obsessing over in the show. "I’m so happy the genealogy scene seemed to land with people," Dippold said about Season 1's penultiamte episode where Rosemary runs down the lengthy ancestry of island founder Richard Warren. "Dale Dickey here memorized that entire thing. I remember the projector screen... I remember it was upside down on the screen so she couldn’t even really use it, she had to to use her mind. Matthew pulled me aside and said, ‘Do you hate Dale Dickey?’"

The Apple TV panel wasn't Widow's Bay's only presence at Comic-Con. At the Showrunners on Showrunning panel Friday afternoon that Dippold participated in alongside Damon Lindelof (Lanterns, Lost) and her former Parks and Recreation boss Greg Daniels (King of the Hill, The Office), the Widow's Bay creator said that she learned the show had been renewed not long before it "became official." She added that the writer's room had started this week and would be active for the next 20 weeks. "The goal is filming early next year."

Other notable reveals from Apple TV's Hall H panel:

Apple TV trotted out a slew of announcements for its first Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday afternoon, including a look at the upcoming second season of Dark Matter, the new Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branaugh movie Mayday, and the back half of SIlo Season 3.

We saw an unexpected release date reveal for its 10-episode Neuromancer series in early 2027. The latest trailer was introduced via video message from its lead Callum Turner, and showunner/executive producer Graham Roland talked about why now was the perfect time to adapt William Gibson's seminal cyperpunk novel.

Hall H got a look at the high-octane trailer for the Matchbox movie (across multiple screens), along with a bit-heavy conversation with the cast where John Cena joked about his fear of doing stunts, which he did for this movie at the request of director Sam Hargrave. "I was scared shitless," told the room. "I like fight choreographym that’s what I feel like I'm fluent at. I hate ledges, I hate heights, I hate cheating death. Each day, I shit my pants. I did a lot of things I'm afraid to do, I conquered none of my fears."

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Project Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

items.title: New Avengers: Doomsday Footage and Poster Revealed at San Diego Comic Con
items.description: Marvel has given fans a new look at Avengers: Doomsday with a fresh poster of Victor Von Doom and an extra clip from the movie showing off his evil abilities.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Marvel has given fans a new look at Avengers: Doomsday with a fresh poster of Victor Von Doom and an extra clip from the movie showing off his evil abilities.

As shown at the Hall H panel on Satuday, July 25, Marvel unveiled a new Doomsday poster showing Doom walking forward, covered in shadows. He looks more menacing than ever, something that holds true to the footage attendees saw that evening.

In an exclusive clip from Doomsday, we see the iconic villain raising up an army of dormant Sentinels - one of the most comic-accurate shots we've had in the MCU.

Doomsday is coming.

Experience Avengers: Doomsday in theaters December 18th. Get tickets now: https://t.co/2HHPv9oLiV pic.twitter.com/WoWRgwW9ut

— Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) July 26, 2026

That same clip features a voice over from Sue Storm, saying, "Victor was always the smartest guy. He used to be kind, he used to be caring. Everything he loved was taken from him. He was broken."

Fans were then shown intense shots of Thor, Shang-Chi, Shuri, and Gambit.

Reed Richards says, "Victor, did you do this?"

Doom answers: "All of you... have stolen lives. But now, you must give them back."

Fans were also treated to a humorous clip of Punisher and Spider-Man taking on the Hulk together in Brand New Day, but it's possible that this isn't the Hulk we know and love. Our reporter on the scene described this version of the Hulk as a sort of hybrid between sensible and savage, both angry and growling while also able to hold a coherent conversation in Banner's voice.

This was just one of three big reveals that night; Ryan Gosling was confirmed to play Ghost Rider in a new movie, while Black Panther III was also confirmed, with David Jonsson taking on the mantle.

Doomsday is coming up fast on December 18, 2026, but Black Panther III is slated for a December 15, 2028 release date.

For more Marvel coverage from the weekend, check out our Live Blog, where we published all the news we learned from the Hall H panel as it happened.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Black Panther 3 Release Date Confirmed by Marvel, With David Jonsson Cast as T'Challa's Son | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Marvel has made Black Panther 3 official, and confirmed it will launch on December 15, 2028.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Marvel has made Black Panther 3 official, and confirmed it will launch on December 15, 2028.

Details of Ryan Coogler's upcoming threequel were discussed today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance.

Notably, British actor David Jonsson was announced as starring in the film as the son of T'Challa, previously seen as a child in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, who is set to inherit the Black Panther title. Jonsson previously appeared in Alien: Romulus and The Long Walk.

Letitia Wright will return as Shuri, while Winston Duke will reprise his role as M'Baku. So both of them presumably survive Avengers: Secret Wars, then.

For a movie that Marvel had previously not officially confirmed, we actually did know a fair bit about the project before today. Coogler had made no secret of the fact that Denzel Washington is involved after revealing he had written a part specifically for him (and this was back in 2024!). Following this revelation, Kevin Feige then admitted that Black Panther 3 was being planned.

"Denzel is family at this point," Coogler said previously. "I've been trying to work with him since day one. I think he's the greatest living actor. In terms of what he means to our culture? Forget about it, man."

A third entry in the hit MCU Black Panther series had always seemed assured after the first entry hit $1.35 billion and its follow-up Wakanda Forever, which was retooled after the tragic death of original Black Panther star Chadwick Boseman, earned another $859 million.

For all the other news and announcements from Hall H, catch up with everything announced at Marvel Studios; Comic Con 2026 panel right here.

Image credit: Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images

items.title: Deadpool and Peggy Carter Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Ryan Reynolds and Hayley Atwell will reprise their Marvel roles as Deadpool and Peggy Carter in Avengers: Doomsday, it's been confirmed.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Ryan Reynolds and Hayley Atwell will reprise their Marvel roles as Deadpool and Peggy Carter in Avengers: Doomsday, it's been confirmed.

Both actors appeared on stage today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance. Deadpool now wears a grey suit, which Reynolds referred to as his "Canadian tuxedo."

"Longtime listener, first time caller," Reynolds said, in character as Deadpool, dropping in on the Marvel panel. "I'm a huge fan. I’m not wearing a Doom mask over this mask because I don’t want to ruin the lines of my Canadian tuxedo," he continued, referencing the plastic Doctor Doom masks handed out to everyone in the audience.

Deadpool (or Reynolds?) continued his bit by asking Avengers: Doomsday's directors Joe and Antony Russo when they were beginning to film the movie, so he could drop by and make a cameo. The brothers told Deadpool/Reynolds that the film was already in the can, though they were still tinkering with it.

Jokes aside, it is very safe to say that Deadpool will be in the film, and very likely to assume that Reynolds' scenes were already shot.

For all the news and announcements from Hall H, catch up with everything announced at Marvel Studios; Comic Con 2026 panel right here.

items.title: Marvel Announces Ryan Gosling Ghost Rider Movie | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Marvel has announced a Ghost Rider movie starring Ryan Gosling, directed by Deadpool & Wolverine's Shawn Levy.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Marvel has announced a Ghost Rider movie starring Ryan Gosling, directed by Deadpool & Wolverine's Shawn Levy.

First details of the project were confirmed today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance. While the film is still a little ways off — it will launch in 2028 — audiences were treated to Gosling and Levy appearing on-stage to discuss the film.

The pair previously worked together filming next year's Star Wars: Starfighter. The fact that Disney is keen for them to re-team again so quickly is likely a promising sign for that film.

The Ghost Rider logo has been revealed at #SDCC, alongside the reveal that Shawn Levy is directing, and it's coming in 2028 pic.twitter.com/L73OqdX51P

— IGN (@IGN) July 26, 2026

Back in March, Ryan Gosling confirmed he'd had discussions with Marvel to play the flame-headed hero Ghost Rider, though said at the time that it was "a complicated situation."

Gosling first mentioned his desire to play Marvel's demonic bike rider back in 2022, which Feige responded positively to at the time. "Hey man, if Ryan wants to be Ghost Rider... Gosling's unbelievable," the Marvel Studios president told MTV News. "Ryan is amazing... I'd love to find a place for him in the MCU."

For all the other news and announcements from Hall H, catch up with everything announced at Marvel Studios; Comic Con 2026 panel right here.

items.title: Yaga Trailer Reveals New Series' Horror and Seductive Side
items.author: Jessie Wade
items.content:
The upcoming thriller series Yaga debuted their long-awaited teaser trailer at San Diego Comic-Con during their panel on Saturday, which you can watch below.

The trailer opens with Carrie-Anne Moss (The Matrix) who plays Katherine, a university professor, telling the tale of Baba Yaga to a young playboy-type man, Henry Park, played by Hudson Williams – who looks utterly enthralled by the story.

As the trailer goes on, you see Noah Reid (Schitt's Creek) as Rapp, a private investigator who's trying to solve the disappearance of Henry, and Clark Backo as local detective Carson. More twists seem to come about as things unfold, with Rapp seemingly getting caught up in Baba Yaga's charm and magic, and Henry unleashing intense feelings throughout.

Yaga is based on the play by Kat Sandler, who serves as Showrunner and Executive Producer. The series is a reimagining of the Slavic folktale of Baba Yaga, but is intended to be a darker, sexy, thriller. It's an original series by Canadian streamer Crave, which gained global popularity with Heated Rivarly in late 2025.

Yaga is set to release in October 2026 on AMC+ for US streamers.

Stay tuned to IGN for more reveals from Yaga and the cast at San Diego Comic-Con, and check out everything announced so far at SDCC 2026!

items.title: Exclusive: Coyote vs. Acme Is Getting a Physical Home Media Release with NSFW John Cena Outtakes | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Coyote vs. Acme director Dave Green confirmed to IGN that the film is coming to Blu-ray, along with some hilarious outtakes that he described as “not PG-rated.”
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Coyote vs. Acme director Dave Green confirmed to IGN that the film is coming to Blu-ray, along with some hilarious outtakes that he described as “not PG-rated.”

We got the chance to chat with Green, as well as Coyote vs. Acme star Lana Condor, at San Diego Comic-Con, where the two gushed about the hilarious moments that happened when John Cena and Will Forte were on set interacting with the Looney Tunes.

“John is an amazing improviser,” Green said. “The camera would keep rolling and he would just love to entertain a room of background actors and make everyone laugh. When you don’t call ‘cut,’ there is minutes and minutes of stuff that is not PG-Rated.”

“Maybe for the Blu-ray,” IGN host Tom Jorgensen replied. “Fingers crossed!”

“I can actually make you that promise,” Green answered. “It’ll be on there.”

In an age where physical media is gradually being phased out in favor of digital downloads, the idea of owning a tangible object that you can play or watch without an internet connection is becoming more and more coveted.

Perhaps the greatest example of this is Sony’s decision to stop printing physical game discs starting January 2028 — a choice that has left the gaming community in disarray, scrambling to get their hands on PlayStation’s final physical releases before the cutoff date.

While some big releases are confirmed for a full physical release, others, like the highly anticipated GTA 6, will have a digital download only (though you can still buy the box that the code comes in, if that counts).

Coyote vs. Acme releases in theaters on August 28, 2026 — a welcome development after it was notably shelved by Warner Bros. Discovery in 2023 for a $30 billion tax write-off. Now audiences can see the movie in its entirety, along with a few R-rated special features when it comes to Blu-ray.

items.title: Rockstar Co-Founder Says 'if People Want' Physical Game Releases Then 'Companies Should Provide It'
items.description: Rockstar Games co-founder Dan Houser believes that, if players want their games released on physical media, then "companies should provide it."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Rockstar Games co-founder Dan Houser believes that, if players want their games released on physical media, then "companies should provide it."

The former Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption developer opened up about the state of physical media in the gaming space during a conversation with IGN at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026. He didn't have a strong opinion when asked if he personally cares about physical versus digital releases, but when it comes to others, his thoughts were pretty cut and dry.

"I don't know that I care, but if people want that, I think companies should provide it," Houser said. "But I don't know that I personally care.

"I also think that, as critical as people are of digital releases, the ability to update and fix problems in games has been really useful for the quality of games."

The question arrives as gamers of every background take to social media to sound off about recent changes in the physical and digital gaming space. PlayStation has found itself in headlines for weeks after confirming it would cease production of new physical games starting in January 2028. Funnily enough, Rockstar has also been involved in the conversation, with Grand Theft Auto fans still coming to terms with confirmation that GTA 6 will not ship on a disc when it launches this November.

Lazlow Jones, who worked with Houser at Rockstar before leaving to join him at Absurd Ventures, was also in attendance at SDCC. In his response to the question, he explained his relationship with both physical and digital games.

"We all have that sort of feeling when you get that copy, and you put the disc in the console, but I also have to say I really like being at the airport and going, 'Oh, cool. I can download some quick games to my Steam Deck for this 12-hour flight.'

"That's what's been interesting. We've worked in digital together for a lot of years, and then making a physical product of a comic book is a different creative process but also just really fulfilling to have a physical thing you can say, 'Look. We made a thing.'"

Houser interjected: "I love physical media."

The Rockstar co-founder isn't the first developer to share his thoughts about the state of physical media. Nier creator Yoko Taro, Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima, and Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot are just a few of the names who have chimed in with thoughts recently.

For now, Houser is at Absurd Ventures, a company he founded and officially announced in 2023. For more on his thoughts on the industry, you can see what he had to say about how people play open-world games.

Photo by Chelsea Guglielmino/Getty Images.

items.title: Neuromancer Release Date, First Look Revealed for Apple TV | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Apple TV's Neuromancer finally has a release date, along with a fast-paced first look at the highly-anticipated cyberpunk series.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Apple TV's Neuromancer finally has a release date, along with a fast-paced first look at the highly anticipated cyberpunk series.

As revealed during the Apple TV panel in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, Neuromancer will come to the streaming service on Friday, January 22, 2027.

Showrunner and executive producer Graham Roland gave fans a few more details on what they can expect from the first-ever screen adaptation of William Gibson's genre-defining novel, explaining why now is the perfect time to bring it to life.

"42 years ago, this book felt like true science fiction," Roland said. "Gibson famously coined the term 'cyberspace' to describe a digital space where people in the book go to to escape and interact [with each other], and he did all that before the internet existed.

"He wrote about the collision of artificial intelligence and human intelligence before artificial intelligence existed. Now, we’re living in a world 40 years later where these things are a part of our everyday lives. It's an appropriate time to revisit the text, to put it in a new light now that these things are here."

Roland also shed some light on what it's been like working with Callum Turner, who plays the book's central character and resident console cowboy, Case. Notably, Roland said that Turner has a big love for Neuromancer, and confirmed that this series is focused on Case.

"He wrote about the collision of artificial intelligence and human intelligence before artificial intelligence existed. Now, we're living in a world where these things are part of our everyday lives."

"Everyone came with a deep love of the source material," he said. "He read the book, dove into his character. Case is an atypical protagonist. He's a criminal, rough around the edges, he’s a survivor. In the book, there's no mention of his family, he’s kind of an orphan, doing out of an instinct of survival, desperation. Callum threads that needle. He's able to play the dangerous part of Case, inhabit the humanity and charisma. One of the things that's very important is that this is Case’s story, you’re following him. The charisma needs to carry you for 10 episodes."

While Turner wasn't physically present at the Comic-Con panel, he did send a video message, which glitched out and eventually lead to a teaser of the show.

"We're building something special with Neuromancer," Turner said. "[Gibson] didn’t just give us cyberspace, he helped us define the entire cyperpunk genre. This is just your first access point."

"The future is in your mind."

Check out the official teaser for Apple TV's Neuromancer. #SDCC pic.twitter.com/gOqHiavOpv

— IGN (@IGN) July 25, 2026

The trailer, which is now live on YouTube, shows a good look at Briana Middleton as Molly with her mirror eyes and deadly fingernails that earn her the moniker 'razorgirl,' the cyberpunk setting of the story, and, of course, Mark Strong as Armitage. It's dark, gritty, and intense.

This is the latest big reveal for Neuromancer after Apple TV+ shared a first look at the series with a 25-second clip two weeks ago. In the clip, someone (presumably Case) pushes a button on a retro computer console. The camera then pans up to a TV screen, which displays the words 'Ashpool-1' and the opening line of Gibson's novel: "The sky above the port was the color of television, tuned to a dead channel."

Gibson himself is executive producer of the show alongside Roland, JD Dillard, and Jennifer Haley. Dillard directed the first three episodes of the series, two of which will premier on Apple TV starting January 22, 2027. Episodes drop weekly on Friday through March 19, 2027. There are ten episodes in all.

items.title: Dungeons & Dragons Movie Sequel Has a Script But 'Financial Reasons' Might Keep It from Ever Coming Out
items.description: Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves co-director Jonathan Goldstein says the script for a sequel already exists, but he's not expecting it to see the light of day any time soon.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves co-director Jonathan Goldstein says the script for a sequel already exists, but he's not expecting it to see the light of day any time soon.

The filmmaker behind the 2023 D&D adaptation gave fans an unfortunate update when speaking with ScreenRant at San Diego Comic-Con (SDCC) 2026. Fans praised the original movie for how it faithfully brought the classic tabletop roleplaying game to the big screen, but it doesn't sound like its favorable reception from critics and audiences will do much to bring a sequel to life.

"We actually wrote a sequel to Dungeons and Dragons," Goldstein said. "We were hired to write it. I don't know that it will see the light of day for a number of financial reasons. They're expensive movies to make, but it'd be great fun to do it. We love that cast, and we think we wrote something that fans would like."

Those "financial reasons" he mentioned are probably a reference to Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves' box office returns. Despite rolling into its opening weekend as the number one movie in theaters domestically, its final global total saw it bring in just $205.46 million (via Box Office Mojo). It’s a respectable enough finish on its own, but considering Variety reported the film cost $150 million before factoring in marketing costs, things could have gone much, much better for the D&D movie.

Still, the fact a sequel script was written suggests someone at Paramount was interested in keeping the story going at some point. The original film – which starred Chris Pine (Edgin), Michelle Rodriguez (Holga), Justice Smith (Simon), Sophia Lillis (Doric), Hugh Grant (Forge), and Regé-Jean Page (Xenk) – has certainly managed to garner a group of die-hard fans since its premiere.

Its Rotten Tomatoes scores, for example, sit at 91% from critics and 92% from fans. IGN gave the film a 7/10 review, calling it an "accessible fantasy adventure that both roasts and respects D&D culture without losing newcomers along for the ride."

With a script on the table and Paramount going through its own changes every day, it's unclear if Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves sequel will ever come to be. Former Paramount Pictures CEO Brian Robbins had previously stated he would be interested in doing a second movie, but only if it could be made "for less." Pine, meanwhile, said in 2023 that he was "pretty confident" it would happen eventually.

items.title: The Most Anticipated Warhammer 40,000 Animation Ever Finally Has a Release Date
items.description: Games Workshop has finally given Warhammer 40,000 fans the news they’ve craved for years: a release date for animated series Astartes 2.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Games Workshop has finally given Warhammer 40,000 fans the news they’ve craved for years: a release date for animated series Astartes 2.

In a post on Warhammer Community, Games Workshop said Astartes 2 is set to drop this December. Via a new promo video, we also have two new shots of Astartes 2, which you can see in the slideshow below. Don't expect a huge amount from the images though, they don't give away much. And there's still much we don't know about Astartes 2 itself. How many episodes will it be? How long will the episodes be? Will it even be divided up into episodes this time?

For the uninitiated, the original Astartes was created by superfan Syama Pedersen, who was subsequently brought into the fold to make the official sequel. In November last year, Games Workshop revealed animation work on a monitor screen via the promo video below, showing a squad of Terminators appearing to protect an unnamed human soldier. This is the Inquisition-led Deathwatch Terminator squad from the debut Astartes 2 teaser in incomplete form, but we know from their pauldron chapter symbols that they’re the same as before (Retributors, Mortifactors, Scythes of The Emperor, Sons of Medusa, and Angels Vermilion).

Astartes is widely accepted as the greatest Warhammer 40,000 animation ever made, official or unofficial, with only Amazon’s excellent Space Marine 2 animation for the Secret Level anthology series competing with it in quality terms. Indeed, Astartes was so good that it inspired Saber Interactive’s hugely successful Space Marine 2 in terms of the look and feel of the Space Marines themselves.

Fans hadn’t heard a peep out of Games Workshop on Astartes 2 for years, leading some to wonder whether the company had quietly cancelled it. But in January last year Games Workshop released a teaser trailer alongside a 2026 release window, and now we know it will be out this December. GW managed to get it in before the end of the year just in time!

Last year’s teaser suggested an animation on a scale and quality never-before-seen from Warhammer 40,000, with melee combat, shooting, vehicle combat, and even spaceship battles all showcased. It showed a number of Space Marine chapters in battle across varied environments, and multiple enemy races, including Tyranids, Orks, and Tau.

But it turned out that nothing in the teaser is actually in the Astartes 2 animation itself. According to a post on the Warhammer Community website: “This teaser trailer is not actually clips from the new animation, instead showing a compilation of shots that represent the former lives of the characters that will appear in the show. There’s a pretty unsubtle hint at the end as to the nature of the final story... We’ll leave you to speculate and start putting the pieces together yourselves.”

Astartes 2 will be available via Games Workshop's streaming service, Warhammer TV.
